Best known for starring as [[Edmund Pevensie]] in [[The Chronicles of Narnia (film series)|''The Chronicles of Narnia'']] film series, he appeared in all three instalments: ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe|The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe]],'' ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian|Prince Caspian]]'', and ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader|The Voyage of the Dawn Treader]]''.[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0363771/ The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe]; [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0499448/ The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian]; [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0980970/ The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader]. ''Internet Movie Database'', retrieved 18 July 2011 == Early life == Keynes was born on 5 September 1991 in [[Camden Town|Camden, London]] to a English father ([[Randal Keynes]]) a author and a [[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] mother (Zelfa Hourani).{{cite web |title=Skandar Keynes, The British Celebrity Who Wants to Be Recognized as Lebanese |website=The961 |date=2019-04-22 |url=https://the961.com/skandar-keynes-british-celebrity-lebanese/ }} He has an older sister, [[Soumaya Keynes|Soumaya]], a journalist and economist, who was the Britain economics editor at ''[[The Economist]]'' magazine{{Cite web|title=Soumaya Keynes|url=https://mediadirectory.economist.com/people/soumaya-keynes/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214093901/https://mediadirectory.economist.com/people/soumaya-keynes/|archive-date=14 December 2021|access-date=2021-12-12|website=Economist}} and is currently an economics columnist at the ''[[Financial Times]]''.{{Cite web |title=Soumaya Keynes |url=https://www.ft.com/soumaya-keynes |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=www.ft.com |language=en-GB}} They grew up in [[Islington, London]]. === Ancestry === On his father's side, Keynes is of English descent, and is the grandson of physiologist [[Richard Keynes]], the nephew of two Cambridge professors, the historian [[Simon Keynes]], and the neuroscientist [[Roger Keynes]], the cousin of Catholic writer and apologist Laura Keynes,West, Ed (2013-06-13). [http://www.catholicherald.co.uk/news/2013/06/13/descendant-of-darwin-becomes-a-catholic-apologist/ Descendant of Darwin Becomes a Catholic Apologist]. ''[[The Catholic Herald]]''. Retrieved 2013-07-09.{{Cite web|date=2013-06-26|title=I'm a Direct Descendant of Darwin...and a Catholic|url=https://strangenotions.com/darwin-catholic/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212162134/https://strangenotions.com/darwin-catholic/|archive-date=12 December 2021|access-date=2021-12-12|website=Strange Notions|language=en}} and the great-great-nephew of economist [[John Maynard Keynes]]. His great-great-great-grandfather was naturalist [[Charles Darwin]]. Keynes' great-grandparents were [[Nobel Prize]] laureate [[Edgar Adrian, 1st Baron Adrian]] and [[Hester Adrian, Baroness Adrian]].Peter Townend, ed., [[Burke's Peerage and Baronetage]], 105th edition (London, U.K.: Burke's Peerage Ltd, 1970), page 27. On his mother's side, Keynes is of [[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] descent.{{Cite web |date=2015-11-09 |title=Skandar Keynes - Interviews Personal Facts |url=http://www.skandar-keynes.com/interviews_item.php?id=8 |access-date=2021-12-13 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109155258/http://www.skandar-keynes.com/interviews_item.php?id=8 |archive-date=9 November 2015 |url-status=dead}} His maternal grandfather was Lebanese writer Cecil Fadlo Hourani, who was an advisor to the late [[President of Tunisia|Tunisian president]] [[Habib Bourguiba]]. The Hourani family were immigrants to [[Manchester]] from [[Marjeyoun]] in southern Lebanon. Cecil's two brothers were [[Albert Hourani]], a historian of the Middle East, and [[George Hourani]], philosopher, historian, and classicist. [[Lebanese nationality law]] states that citizenship is passed on patrilineally, so Keynes is legally a foreigner in the country he considers his second home.{{cite news |last= Elali |first= Nadine |title= A second home in Lebanon: Talking to Skandar Keynes |work= [[NOW Lebanon]] |location= Beirut, Lebanon |date= 29 September 2012 |url= http://www.nowlebanon.com/NewsArticleDetails.aspx?ID=441454&MID=0&PID=0 |access-date= 13 October 2012 |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20121006134305/http://www.nowlebanon.com/NewsArticleDetails.aspx?ID=441454 |archive-date= 6 October 2012 |df= dmy-all }} == Education == Keynes attended the [[Anna Scher Theatre|Anna Scher Theatre School]], after going to Thornhill Primary School. December 2021|access-date=2021-12-12|website=en.24smi.org|language=en}} Keynes achieved international prominence in the role of [[Edmund Pevensie]] in the major motion picture ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe]]'' (2005) directed by [[Andrew Adamson]]. Shot predominantly in New Zealand and a few in Central Europe, it was released in December 2005 to critical and high commercial success, grossing more than $745 million worldwide. In 2004, after the producers saw 2,000 young hopefuls, Keynes won the role of Edmund whose story is especially dramatic as his character is central to themes of betrayal, forgiveness, and redemption. He performed his own complex stunts: jumping into the ditch, sword fighting, and horse riding. He also voiced his character in the video game ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (video game)|The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe]]''. In 2006, Keynes was awarded the [[CAMIE Awards|CAMIE Award]] (Character and Morality in Entertainment) for his portrayal. He reprised his role as Edmund in ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian|Prince Caspian]],'' directed by Andrew Adamson and released in May 2008 to generally positive reviews, grossing $419.7 million worldwide. He enjoyed the action-oriented stuntwork, touring New Zealand, Prague, Slovenia, Poland, and Czech Republic within seven months of shooting.{{cite web|author=Utichi, Joe|date=25 June 2008|title=RT Interview: Skandar Keynes on the Action Challenge of Prince Caspian: Edmund Pevensie on the new experiences of the Narnian second part|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/chronicles_of_narnia_prince_caspian/news/1736822/2/rt_interview_skandar_keynes_on_the_action_challenge_of_prince_caspian/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080628182923/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/chronicles_of_narnia_prince_caspian/news/1736822/2/rt_interview_skandar_keynes_on_the_action_challenge_of_prince_caspian/|archive-date=28 June 2008|access-date=10 September 2017|publisher=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]}} For his performance, he was nominated for Best Performance in a Feature Film – Leading Young Actor and Best Performance in a Feature Film – Young Ensemble Cast at the [[Young Artist Awards 2009|30th Young Artist Awards]]. Keynes also voiced his character in the video game [[The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (video game)|''The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian'']]. He returned as Edmund in ''[[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader|The Voyage of the Dawn Treader]]'', the third instalment of [[The Chronicles of Narnia (film series)|''The Chronicles of Narnia'']], directed by [[Michael Apted]], filmed in Australia and released in December 2010, grossing $415.7 million worldwide. In preparation, Keynes trained to earn his [[Professional Association of Diving Instructors]] license for underwater scenes.{{cite web|author=Nemiroff, Perri|date=2010-12-06|title=Interview: The Chronicles Of Narnia's Skandar Keynes|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/new/Interview-The-Chronicles-Of-Narnia-s-Skandar-Keynes-22052.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170924092624/http://www.cinemablend.com/new/Interview-The-Chronicles-Of-Narnia-s-Skandar-Keynes-22052.html|archive-date=24 September 2017|access-date=13 October 2012|publisher=Cinema Blend}} In 2011, the cast was nominated for Best Performance in a Feature Film – Young Ensemble Cast at the [[32nd Young Artist Awards|Young Artist Awards 2011]]. 2016 |url-status=dead}} ===Politics=== In January 2015, Keynes completed a three-month internship at the [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]]. During his stay in [[Amman|Amman, Jordan]], he assisted in the research and writing of ''Living in the Shadows: Jordan Home Visits Report 2014,'' a study that found evidence of a rapid deterioration in the living conditions of Syrian refugees in Jordan as the [[Syrian civil war|Syrian conflict]] entered its fifth year.{{Cite web |date=2018-10-29 |title=Skandar Keynes - News A Three-Month Internship at UNHCR |url=http://www.skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=31 |access-date=2021-12-13 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181029083602/http://www.skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=31 |archive-date=29 October 2018 |url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|title=Living in the shadows: Jordan Home Visits Report 2014 - Jordan|url=https://reliefweb.int/report/jordan/living-shadows-jordan-home-visits-report-2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214103657/https://reliefweb.int/report/jordan/living-shadows-jordan-home-visits-report-2014|archive-date=14 December 2021|access-date=2021-12-13|website=ReliefWeb|date=14 January 2015 |language=en}} The report is based on data from home visits covering almost 150,000 Syrian refugees living outside of camps in Jordan. Published on January 14, 2015, it has been widely reported in the media and cited by foreign policy think tanks.{{Cite web|last=UNHCR|first=United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees|date=2015-01-14|title=Living in the shadows - His interview with wolf expert Jean-Marc Landry and deputy head Jean-Christophe Viẻ is featured on Wild Talk Radio Podcast.{{Cite web|date=March 25, 2009|title=Grey Wolf in the Jura Mountains, Switzerland|url=http://skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=20|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815075529/http://skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=20|archive-date=August 15, 2016|access-date=December 21, 2021|website=Skandar-keynes.com}} In March 2009, he contributed to [[English Heritage]] by writing the foreword to the [[Charles Darwin|Darwin]] issue of the ''Heritage Learning Journal (Issue 40)''.{{Cite web|title=Skandar Keynes Brasil|url=https://www.facebook.com/SkandarKeynesBR/photos/a.320240311451457/320240328118122/?type=3|access-date=2021-12-20|website=www.facebook.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Darwin Online: Darwin 2009 commemorations around the world|url=http://darwin-online.org.uk/2009.html?newwindow=true|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20211220202556/http://darwin-online.org.uk/2009.html?newwindow=true|archive-date=December 20, 2021|access-date=2021-12-20|website=darwin-online.org.uk}} He also promoted connect2earth, an online community run by [[World Wide Fund for Nature]].{{Cite web|date=2009-04-06|title=Con la comunidad connect2earth, ahora jóvenes y expertos ambientales de renombre podrán debatir cuestiones ecológicas|url=https://www.iucn.org/node/3599|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20211220203024/https://www.iucn.org/node/3599|archive-date=December 20, 2021|access-date=2021-12-20|website=IUCN|language=en}} He joined his father in the Galapagos Tortoise Project by promoting Sebastian, one of the largest of the giant tortoises conserved by the archipelago's national park.{{Cite web |date=2016-08-15 |title=Skandar Keynes - News Sebastian Keynes the Giant Tortoise |url=http://skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=22 |access-date=2021-12-20 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815080242/http://skandar-keynes.com/news_item.php?id=22 |archive-date=15 August 2016 |url-status=dead}} === Lebanon === Keynes and his family have been visiting [[Marjeyoun]] in [[Lebanon]] yearly, despite the political situation, since he was a child. "I was here in 1996 during [[Operation Grapes of Wrath]]. I was four at the time and had no concept that it was war," Keynes told a reporter. "I remember when the gravity of the situation dawned on me. It was during the [[2006 Lebanon War|2006 July war]], I was 14 then... but it didn't really shake my view of Lebanon as effectively a second home, a place where I come to and I have family." Cognisant of the [[Lebanese nationality law]], he expressed, "I understand that in part the law that a mother cannot pass her nationality to her children is tied with the Palestinian issue... I would like to see the law changed and be considered Lebanese by the government. extract: Alexander Amin Caspar Keynes (born 5 September 1991) is an English political adviser and former actor. Best known for starring as Edmund Pevensie in The Chronicles of Narnia film series, he appeared in all three instalments: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Prince Caspian, and The Voyage of the Dawn Treader.
